findings.text: release_answered_holds duplicates the capability reckon/crew/lead_decisions.py:420 release_withdrawn_holds owns -- walk the live held pointers, release the ones a settled decision bound, and write the released phase back into the pointer the pass read -- so a change to the release loop or its phase write-back now has two implementations to keep in step.

the release matches only the answer's recorded held_requests and never checks the pointer's own queue_hold.decision_id, which the owner at reckon/crew/lead_decisions.py:442 does check, so an answer releases a request a coordinator later re-held behind a different decision.

answered_items emits a duty for every answer ever recorded for the same project and session with no condition that retires it, so an owning session collects one permanent obligation row per answer on every read rather than a current duty.

assert saved["choice"] == "wait" compares the record answer_decision returns against the choice this test itself passed in, so it stays green for a regression that echoes the input without persisting it; the independent guards here are the release assertions at lines 199-201.

answer_decision reuses the name reckon/crew/lost_session_work.py:445 already carries for a different capability, and that owner is what the existing crew decision answer command at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:623 imports, so two unrelated answers to a decision now share one name in one package.

the fragment's head arm is quoted at 60983907ec and its probe called advance_waiting_requests, which no longer releases an answered hold since the release moved to reckon/crew/admission/selection.py:265, and the probe is absent from the tree at the delivered head, so the recorded head arm would not reproduce at 5af4c2caf1.
